(This evening through Tuesday)...
Issued at 229 PM EST Tue Nov 24 2026

Surface analysis this afternoon shows strong high pressure centered 
over IA/WI/MN. This strong high was in control of the weather across 
much of the eastern United States. Cool northeast surface flow was 
found across Indiana and temperatures were in the lower 40s. Aloft, 
water vapor shows ridging in place over IL/IN and WI, while a deeper 
trough was found over the western plains. Ridge riding cirrus was 
found over IL and WI pushing east, beginning to invade Indiana. 
Subsidence was still in place across Indiana. GOES19 shows some lake 
cloud across NW Indiana, but this appears to be dissipating.

Tonight through mid day Wednesday...

Clouds are expected to increase during this time as the upper trough 
axis to the west continues to push east. High CI ahead of the trough 
as seen on satellite will continue to stream into Indiana tonight 
and through Wednesday morning. Meanwhile the surface high pressure 
system to the east will continue to provide dry easterly flow within 
the lower levels. This can be seen within the forecast soundings, 
where dry air remains within the lower levels and moisture arrives 
aloft. Thus increasing clouds will be expected tonight. The 
increasing clouds along with slight warm air advection will lead to 
warmer low temperatures as mixing remains in play overnight. Look 
for lows in the upper 20s.

Wednesday Night through Thursday...

An Active weather situation is expected during this period. The 
upper wave to the west with dual upper lows will advance across the 
plains and phase into a deep upper low near the Arkansas/TN boarder. 
The upper low looks to become a negatively tilted system by 
Wednesday night before continuing to deepen and arrive across 
southern Indiana on Thanksgiving. Strong cyclonic flow will be in 
place over Indiana. Mid level moisture will be arriving on Wednesday 
afternoon as a surge arrives from the gulf ahead of the approaching 
low. By Thursday, mid level fetch is deep and extensive, stretching 
from the Atlantic to Indiana and Illinois. Central Indiana will be 
located on the north side of this system, a favorable location for 
moisture and rain. Forecast soundings show deep saturation in play 
on Wednesday overnight through Thursday, with high pwats near 1.00, 
high values for this time of year. Forecast soundings do show a warm 
layer near the surface thru Thursday, but cold air advection and 
dynamic cooling will shrink the depth of that shallow melting layer 
during the evening hours on Thursday. At that time, a few snowflakes 
mixing in with rain will be possible. Forecast soundings never quite 
do show the lowest levels falling below freezing, and actually start 
to warm a bit toward 12Z Friday. 

Overall, high confidence for rain arrival on Wednesday Night and 
continuing through Thursday. Rain amounts of around an inch look 
likely, with higher amounts possible. Thus will have pops during 
this time near 100. Finally, a few snowflakes could mix in across the 
area late on Thursday Night, but accumulations are not expected at 
this time.

Friday through Tuesday...

Unsettled and cooler weather looks to be in play on Black Friday as 
Thursday systems will have departed to the east. However strong 
cyclonic flow will remain in place across Indiana with plentiful 
lower level moisture in place, especially in the morning. This could 
lead to a few morning showers and low pops will still need to be 
included. Subsidence and dry air begin to enter column on Friday 
afternoon as ridging aloft begins to build from the west. This 
should lead to clearing skies through the day.

Ridging aloft on Friday night and early Saturday will bring 
continued dry but mild weather for Friday night into Saturday. By 
Saturday night and Sunday a new and broad area of low pressure will 
be found over northern Ontario, providing weak cyclonic flow across 
Indiana. Models seem to hint at low chance pops with but confidence 
is low due to only Pacific moisture appearing available.

Dry weather is expected on Monday as surface high pressure will be 
in place. More chances for rain will return on Tuesday as another 
short wave is expected to approach Indiana at that time from the 
central plains.
